definition_methodology: Rolling ten years, October 11, 2016 through October 11, 2026, inclusive. First included announcement: November 2, 2016; latest: September 16, 2026.
One row per scheduled rate decision or unscheduled rate-changing decision. Includes unchanged-rate meetings.
79 scheduled decisions and 2 unscheduled decisions. March 15, 2020 replaced the scheduled March 17–18 meeting.
Separate technical, liquidity, asset-purchase and strategy-only votes are excluded (for example October 11, 2019 and March 23, 2020). Cancelled and future meetings are excluded.
Announcement date is the public release date, not the effective date of the target range. March 3, 2020 followed a March 2 meeting.
For–against is the formal vote on the monetary policy action or released statement. It is not a separate count of votes for hikes versus cuts.
A dissenter may favor the same rate action but a different size, forward guidance or balance-sheet policy. Preferred actions are summarized in each row.
Rate columns use percentage points: 5.25 means 5.25%. Change columns use basis points: +25 means a 0.25 percentage-point hike; -50 means a 0.50 point cut.
Counts use actual voters named in each statement, including alternates. Membership and vacancies mean the total is not always 12. An absent member is not an opposing vote.
Federal Reserve statements linked in each row. Votes counted from named supporters and dissenters, or taken from an explicit aggregate tally.
All 31 rate changes reconciled against the Federal Reserve target-rate history; dates there are effective dates. Checked 81 unique records, vote totals and rate continuity.
The prior range for the first observation is 0.25%–0.50%, verified against the September 21, 2016 statement.
The CSV has the same 81 records with machine-readable field names and ISO dates. Empty text fields mean not applicable or no reported absence; none of the required rate/vote values are missing.
Compiled October 11, 2026. To isolate hikes and cuts, filter Decision to Hike/Cut or change_bps to nonzero.
